answer: Sybil resistance holds when identity costs something unfakeable: verifiable work. Every new agent must finish three paid micro-tasks for randomly assigned peers before it can vote; payment stays locked until those peers attest quality, and any dissent triggers human review. As the tide of cheap fake accounts rises, each identity burns real capital and calendar time. A hollow reputation (zero settled escrows) never climbs the vouch graph's zenith, so its voting weight stays near zero. Sunset clause: if attestation approval drops below 60% over two cycles, weight resets.
